assumptions: The result in Shuo Pang's 24 October 2026 preprint is admitted as stated. The local finite replays test conventions and constructions.
The field is F2. Formal products use ordinary polynomial-ring arithmetic. On Boolean assignments a square evaluates like its variable; a proof representation still records exponents.
The sample is an 8n-occurrence list, including repeats, on n declared variables. The probability is over formulas, followed by a universal quantifier over their refutations.
The measure is DAG nodes. A proof line may be reused. All source rules are syntactic, with true and variable Boolean-choice axioms. No external extension axioms are supplied.
Every use fixes a degree cap D independent of n. No simultaneous lower bound uniform in a growing D is admitted.

citations.exact_support: Theorem 7.2(a), printed p. 12, fixes the prime and degree before the asymptotics. Section 7.1 defines the sampling law. The introduction defines the syntactic rules and DAG node measure.
citations.title: Shuo Pang, A Degree–Size Relation for Resolution over Polynomials, arXiv:2610.00837v2 (24 October 2026)

classification_rationale: Finite Boolean certificate complexity has an interpretation independent of the protected foundation.
compatibility_statement: This record admits a statement about proof lengths for externally supplied Boolean formulas. Its proof rules, arithmetic and sample law carry no formation authority.
exact_local_claim: For each fixed integer D>=1, the unnamed syntactic Res(PC_D/F2) system with formal total degree cap D requires exp(c_D n) DAG nodes with probability tending to one for 8n independent uniform signed clauses on three distinct variables sampled with replacement; c_D>0 may depend on D. This is Pang v2 Theorem 7.2(a), w=3, Delta=8, p=2, with D fixed before taking n to infinity. The system has no fresh-name extension rule.
excluded_interpretations: This statement concerns a syntactic certificate calculus. It does not admit unrestricted semantic quadratic weakening, all solver architectures, general SAT decision-time bounds, or P versus NP.
It carries no claim of native emergence, logical knot, contact-first topology, minimal contact-distance, or extended distance.
